values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/baxterbridge ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground', 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Carry-in kayak landing next to site 25; paddle campers can reach the campground from the Manistee River.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/baxterbridge ('There are vault toilets', 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/baxterbridge ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis', 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 25 sites 'for tents and small trailers' among old red pines. No length limit posted. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/baxterbridge ('This campground features 25 sites for tents and small trailers', 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site'), read 2026-10-25

season.source: https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Baxter Bridge State Forest Campground: 'Seasonal closure dates' 'open all year'; 'SFCG campground roads may not be plowed in the winter'), read 2026-10-25

note: Shaded rustic campground among old red pines on the Manistee River, ~12 mi NW of Manton via M-42 and 31 Road; Campendium tags it big-rig friendly. Popular canoe/kayak/tube put-in; trout fishing, and the North Country Trail is a mile away. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 25 sites, $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only, 15-day max, open all year (all confirmed); kayak landing and paddle-in access in facilities.note. Note's '$15/night' (contradicted: $20) dropped with the other field restatements.
